# Roadmap

A box in a lab, modelled from first principles in C++23, for no reason.

<!-- Generated by `cairn render`. The items under cairn/items/ are the source;
     this file is a copy, and copies rot. Do not edit it by hand. -->

The project in order, from a pinhole to a photograph.

Each milestone is a state the repository can be read in — not a feature set. If
you cloned it at any one of them, the thing would build, run, produce an image,
and make exactly the claims it had by then earned. The sequence is deliberate in
one respect above all others: **the instruments of proof are built in v0.5,
before the physics they judge.** A check written after the thing it checks is a
check written to pass.

The two claims the whole roadmap serves are in `CLAUDE.md`, and every item
labelled `thesis` exists to make one of them true or to catch it becoming false.

    cairn next                  what is ready to work on now
    cairn list --view thesis    the items the project exists for
    cairn list --view honesty   admissions owed: what is not modelled

## v0.2 — The cosine law

## v1.4 — Paths from both ends

`··········` 0% · 0 of 4 done

Some light paths are essentially impossible to find by walking backwards from the camera. A caustic under a glass of water is the standard example: the camera sees a bright patch on a table whose brightness depends on a path that must pass through a specular surface in exactly the right place.

## v1.5 — The camera as an object

`··········` 0% · 0 of 5 done

A pinhole has no aberration because it has no glass. Every real camera is a stack of ground surfaces, and everything photographers have vocabulary for — bokeh, coma, vignetting, the way a fast lens renders an out-of-focus highlight as a disc with a bright rim — is that stack being imperfect in a specific way.
